title: Attempts of Transforming Teacher Practice Through Professional Development
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the challenge of improving physics and mathematics teaching through professional development, with the goal of producing lasting changes in classroom practice. The authors argue that teacher development is essential for increasing the quality of science education and, indirectly, student interest and enrolment in scientific fields.

The paper describes a series of professional development activities carried out in southern Tuscany within the Italian National Plan for Scientific Degrees. These activities included long advanced courses for qualified teachers, a summer school in physics where young teachers worked alongside expert teachers, a national master’s program in physics educational innovation, a workshop on modelling for physics and mathematics teachers, and several in-service updating courses held in specific schools. The interventions emphasized laboratory work, joint design of learning paths, interdisciplinary discussion, and opportunities to test materials in class when possible.

The participants were mainly secondary school teachers, many of whom were young and without permanent positions; some activities also involved expert teachers, university staff, and school administrators. The main conclusion is that professional development is most effective when it is context-specific, laboratory-based, and supported by school leadership, but that it is difficult to engage in-service teachers deeply, especially when activities are too intensive or disconnected from school constraints. The authors found that some informal, school-based updating courses worked better than broader or more demanding programs, particularly when teachers had strong management support and immediate relevance to their teaching context.

identified_tools.name: ITS (General)
identified_tools.description: An intelligent tutoring system is an AI-driven educational system that provides guided instruction, practice, and feedback/adaptation to learners.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper does not study an AI tutoring system; it discusses teacher professional development activities in physics and mathematics, including laboratory-based workshops and updating courses.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative/descriptive professional development paper about teacher training activities, not an empirical evaluation of an AI tool. No AI system is studied or compared, so evidence quality for AI tool effects is not applicable.
impact_tier_rationale: There are no measured AI-tool outcomes, effect sizes, or intervention impacts in the paper. The paper reports reflections on professional development formats and implementation challenges only.
